title: [feature] The owner pauses a mission and resumes it: no work assigned or delivered, its resident stopped with its branch and transcript kept, no idle alert or idle hours, and it reads paused
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/missions.rs (`mission`: the verbs, `resume`), crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (`spawn_mission_resume`, `spawn_objective_assign`, the `mission.halted` and `mission.resumed` folds of `mission_missions`), crates/spawn-cli/src/deliver.rs (a retired resident's Stop, `restart_order`), crates/spawn-cli/src/recover.rs (how a Stop's end is recorded), crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs (`mission_idle`, `read_idle`), crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/fleet.rs (`idle`) with crates/spawn-postgres/src/experience.rs (the missions' spans), crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (`/api/missions`), and web/src/missions.ts (`normalizeMissions`), web/src/missionTimeline.ts (`laneState`) and web/src/home.ts (`missionsToday`, `quietText`, `noWorkText`).

The owner's order (2026-11-12 19:20 and 20:00, sync/queue.md lead-mac 20:00, "Mission 6 pause"). It goes ahead of the card rows.

The problem. The owner asked for mission 6 (Supply PA) to be paused. Spawn has no such state. A mission is active, closed (`spawn mission close`, final), or halted, which only the system sets (a raw push, a gate's rejections) and `spawn mission resume` clears. The owner has no verb to hold a mission, and no way to stop its resident short of killing a process by hand, which nobody may do. So mission 6 stays active with no objectives: its resident's engine runs idle, Home raises "A mission has no work" for it, and the Scorecard counts its hours as idle. All three are wrong for a mission the owner chose to hold.

Required behaviour.
(a) `spawn mission pause --id N [--reason <text>]`, for the owner (a human) only, records `mission.paused` {id, reason}. An agent caller is refused, with nothing recorded.
- It refuses, non-zero with nothing recorded, a mission that is closed or already paused.
- A halted mission can be paused: the halt stays as it is.
(b) While a mission is paused:
- No objective is assigned to it: spawn_objective_assign refuses, and its error names the pause. Nothing is delivered to its workers.
- Its resident is stopped by a Stop, at once, as a retired resident is; the Stop takes a final checkpoint. Nothing revives it while the mission is paused. Either way works: the dispatcher's own Stop, which the recovery records as final and the dispatcher resumes at the unpause, as `spawn task restart` does (deliver.rs `restart_order`); or the recovery's `wait` path with a `paused` cause. Its delivered task stays delivered. What is kept: its branch with the final checkpoint, and its engine session (the native transcript). Its workspace directory is removed at the stop, as at any stop, and rebuilt from the branch at the resume; what the checkpoint leaves out is lost, as at any stop.
- No `mission_idle` alert fires for it. An open one clears at the pause, its cleared evidence naming the `mission.paused` record.
- `/api/scorecard/fleet`'s mission row carries `paused_hours`, its paused time within its span. `idle_hours` leaves that time out. A mission paused at the window's end is never flagged `idle`; otherwise it is flagged when idle_hours × 2 > hours − paused_hours.
- `/api/missions` gives the mission `paused` {at_ms, event_id, reason}, or null when it is not paused. Its `state` stays as it was.
(c) `spawn mission resume --id N` on a paused mission records `mission.unpaused` {id, pause_event} and nothing else.
- Assignment and delivery go on. The resident is resumed (a `resume`, once per unpause) in its own native session, on its workspace rebuilt from its branch.
- On a halted mission that is not paused, resume is unchanged.
- On a mission both paused and halted, resume clears only the pause: the halt stays, and a second resume clears it.
(d) web/src:
- missions.ts keeps `paused`.
- missionTimeline.ts `laneState` gives "paused" for a paused mission.
- home.ts `missionsToday` marks a paused mission `paused: true`, both on its row (work in flight) and on its quiet entry (nothing in flight, idle_ms null).
- `quietText` names it "#<id> <name> (paused)".
- `noWorkText` leaves it out of "none for".
- The Missions page and the Home card show "paused" (read off a screenshot).
No gate, integrator or deploy step reads any of it beyond (b).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/099.sh. A real loop and `spawn serve` run four missions. Each takes its work from an objective backlog, with a resident of its own:
- mission 1's resident bbone has a delivered task, whose first turn checkpoints work.txt;
- missions 2 and 3 each had a task, then cancelled;
- mission 4 is closed.
Mission 3 is paused before the 8 s idle bound. Checks:
- (1) The pause of mission 1: exit 0, and one `mission.paused` {id, reason}. /api/missions shows `paused` and state active. A second pause, and a pause of closed mission 4, are refused with nothing recorded.
- (2) bbone's execution ends within 20 s. work.txt stays on its branch, and its transcript stays. No execution starts for 8 s, and its task stays delivered.
- (3) spawn_objective_assign on paused mission 3 refuses, naming the pause.
- (4) Once mission 2 has its open mission_idle (the barrier), paused mission 3 has none. The 24 h Scorecard flags mission 2 idle, not mission 3, whose paused_hours > 0 and idle_hours + paused_hours ≤ hours. web/src under node over /api/missions reads paused for missions 1 and 3, and not for mission 2. Pausing mission 2 then clears its alert, naming the pause.
- (5) The resume of mission 1: exit 0, and one `mission.unpaused` {id, pause_event}; /api/missions shows paused null. bbone starts again within 30 s as a resume of its own native session, finding work.txt. Resumed mission 3 is assigned again.
It fails with 1 on the mission's main 4614e528: there is no pause verb, so nothing below it holds. Its throwaway is in sync/obj-099/.

For live once this lands (a lead step, in this order):
- (1) Print-only: list mission 6's workspace files that are not on its branch (what the pause's stop would not keep).
- (2) If that list is not empty, the lead copies exactly those files into /data/spawn-archive/paused/mission-6-<ts>.tar and records its sha256 in sync/queue.md. This step only copies; it deletes nothing.
- (3) `spawn mission pause --id 6 --reason "owner hold 2026-11-12"`. Its resident agent_resident_supply is then stopped by Spawn itself, not by hand. The "A mission has no work" alert for mission 6 clears, and Home and Missions read paused. Mission 6's branch and transcripts stay, and with (2) no file of its workspace is lost.

The product reason. The owner decides what the fleet works on. Holding a mission without closing it, or killing anything by hand, is a basic control the owner lacks today. Without it, the fleet raises a false alarm and counts idle hours that are the owner's choice.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green (043, 051, 053, 058 and 062 read missions, halts, idle and the Scorecard) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour:
- a spawn-postgres test, through the real store, of `mission.paused` and `mission.unpaused` (the refusals, an agent caller's refusal with nothing recorded among them, the fold, spawn_objective_assign's refusal, and a resume of a mission both paused and halted clearing only the pause);
- a deliver test that a paused mission's resident is stopped and gets nothing;
- an alerts test that a paused mission fires no mission_idle and that the pause clears an open one;
- a scorecard/fleet unit test of paused_hours and the idle flag;
- web/test cases of laneState, missionsToday, quietText and noWorkText for a paused mission.
